title: cust-edge-orchestrator-compact-audit-prd-draft
body:
Overview:

This is a working PRD sketch for a lightweight customer-edge orchestration pattern that minimizes audit payload volume while preserving forensic fidelity and enabling deterministic approval gates. The core idea: when customers operate managed connectivity (customer-managed VPCs / on-prem edge boxes), we provide an "attestation broker" inside the Private control plane that accepts compact proof capsules from the customer edge and either approves or routes change requests based on configurable gates and probabilistic sampling rules.

Background and motivation:
- Customers want private deployments but also need Redwood to satisfy audit and SLA commitments. Shipping full verbose network diffs and packet traces is infeasible for bandwidth and privacy reasons.
- Existing proposals in this folder assume full immutable logs; that increases storage and egress cost and slows onboarding. We need a middle ground: high-integrity, delta-oriented audit capsules + a small set of canonical snapshots.

Goals (high level):
- Provide verifiable, tamper-evident "compact audit capsules" for customer-managed network events (security group updates, peering changes, route table edits, keystore rotation, operator-initiated rollback bundles).
- Expose approval gates that can be configured by customers and operators (time-window SLAs, escalation paths, human-in-the-loop checkpoints) and that operate with low latency.
- Keep default telemetry footprint << full logs (~1-3KB per change) while supporting on-demand forensic replays (pull full traces from customer side when permitted).

Success metrics (candidate):
- Median approval latency for auto-approvals < 150ms for benign changes in baseline load tests.
- Audit payloads compressed median size < 2.5KB/change.
- Forensic pull success rate > 99% when customer allows remote fetch.
- Reduction in egress storage compared to naive full-log model by > 70%.

Scope (in):
- Compact capsule format design and signing semantics.
- Approval gate DSL and runtime: basic policies (whitelist/blacklist, time-window, rate-limit, probabilistic sampling for deep audits), canary templates.
- Operator UX in the Console for triage, evidence inspection, and manual approval.
- End-to-end test harness (simulated customer edges and replay).

Out of scope (for this draft):
- Deep integration with KMS/HSM (we will link to existing KMS PRD).
- Long-term cold forensic archive design (follow-up project).

Key concepts and constraints:
- Compact Audit Capsule: a small JSON blob representing a change: {event_type, normalized-delta, timestamp, edge-epoch, capsule-hash, signer-cert}. Capsules should be canonicalized and signed by an edge key. We use delta encoding and stable field ordering to make proofs reproducible.
- Snapshot Anchors: periodic full snapshots (daily or on-demand) that can be referenced by capsules (snapshot_id + diff_offset). Customers may opt into more frequent snapshots.
- Attestation Broker: Redwood control-plane service that verifies capsule signatures, validates schema, computes risk score (heuristic + ML model later), and either auto-approves, escalates, or rejects the change per policy.

Approval Gate Design (first pass):
- Policy DSL primitives: allow/deny patterns, role-bound approvers, SLA timeout, sample-rate for deep-audit, fallback-model (e.g., use compatible model variant or reject).
- Two-phase approval option: phase 1 = compact-capsule validation + quick checks; phase 2 = on-demand fetch + human review for sampled items.
- Canary rollouts: customer can tag change-classes as canary; first N changes in an epoch pass through stricter sampling.

Data model / schema notes (implementation guidance only):
- Keep capsule shape minimal; avoid embedding full keys or secrets. Include references to customer-side storage endpoints (S3 URI or edge file handle) for full traces.
- Include transient witness (edge-provided ephemeral nonce) to prevent replay.
- Support two signing modes: edge-signed and operator-signed (for operator-initiated actions where edge attestation is absent).

Operator and Customer UX flows:
- Default autopilot: low-risk changes auto-approve; customers get digest emails and console timeline entries.
- Manual review flow: approver sees capsule summary + risk score + quick diff (normalized delta). Option to request full trace — triggers a pull that must be allowed by customer policy (consent flags).
- Emergency bypass process with audit penalty token (used when SLA demands immediate action). Bypass must produce a heightened capsule (with operator identity, justification, and TTL).

Privacy and compliance considerations:
- Capsule design favors metadata-only proofs and references to where full data can be fetched with customer consent.
- For regulated customers, default policy should be "no remote pulls" unless explicit contract (this is a product configuration toggle).

Migration for existing private deployments:
- Phase A: opt-in beta where customers install an edge agent that emits capsules alongside existing verbose logs.
- Phase B: allow customers to switch to compact-only mode once sampling and snapshot syncs verified.

Open engineering questions / risks:
- How to guarantee capsule correlation with full-trace fetches when customer deletes traces? Need retention contract or snapshot escrow.
- Tamper/equivocation: edges could produce inconsistent capsule sequences if compromised. Consider checkpointed snapshot anchors anchored in Redwood control plane or customer HSM.
- Performance under high-change-rate tenants: broker must remain stateless enough to horizontally scale; consider batching capsule validation and streaming verification workers.

Implementation milestones (proposal):
- Week 1-2: finalize capsule schema and signing protocol; mock broker validation service.
- Week 3-6: implement policy DSL prototype and console UI mockups for approvals; simple simulator for sample-rate experiments.
- Week 7-10: beta integration with 2 pilot customers; measure payload sizes and approval latencies.

Open questions for product review:
- Default sampling rate for deep audits? (start 0.5% and iterate?)
- Snapshot cadence tradeoffs (daily vs hourly) and pricing model for extra snapshots.
- What is minimum operator accountability info for emergency bypass that legal will accept?

Next steps:
- Review with SRE and Security for feedback on signing/key assumptions (action: Diego Morales).
- Build prototype capsule encoder + verifier and run 10k-change/day simulation (action: Priya Nair).
- Draft contract language for snapshot escrow and remote fetch consent (legal touchpoint request).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add example capsule payloads and canonicalization code snippet in appendix.
- Link to relevant KMS PRD and network forensic guidelines.

This doc is intentionally lightweight and meant to capture the design tradeoffs before committing to a full-fledged immutable-log approach. Feedback welcome; aim to iterate into an RFC for Q1 planning.
